tagline: Java's own marine-park archipelago — reached today only by a slow, weather-bound crossing of the open Java Sea.
summary: Karimunjawa is a 27-island national-marine-park archipelago in the Java Sea, the closest tropical island cluster to Central Java's millions. Getting there today means a weather-exposed open-sea crossing — a ~2-hour fast ferry from Semarang or a ~6-hour slow ro-pax from Jepara — both of which routinely cancel in the wet-season swell. Once you arrive, the islands sit a calm 3–10 nm apart over protected reef water. That combination — a fragile, slow gateway crossing plus short, sheltered intra-archipelago hops inside a clean-marine conservation zone — is exactly where smooth, reliable, zero-emission foiling transforms the trip.

use_cases.title: Reliable mainland gateway crossing
use_cases.body: Replace the weather-fragile Semarang/Jepara ferry with an all-electric foiling shuttle on the ~45–50 nm open-sea legs — smoother, dramatically less prone to wet-season cancellation, and far more comfortable than the pounding ro-pax.

use_cases.title: Clean intra-archipelago island-hopping
use_cases.body: Short 3–10 nm hops between Karimun Besar, Menjangan, Kemujan (Kura Kura Resort) and the snorkel/dive islets, run quietly and wake-free over protected reef water — modernising the wooden longboat day-trip with a zero-emission fleet inside the marine park.

use_cases.title: Mainland-city direct escape
use_cases.body: A long-range hybrid run from Jakarta or Surabaya direct to the archipelago over the sheltered interior Java Sea, turning a multi-modal fly-then-ferry day into a single smooth passage for premium leisure travellers.

journeys.today: ~2-hour fast ferry across open water that cancels in wet-season squalls; slower 6-hour ro-pax from Jepara is the fallback.
journeys.with_navier: An all-electric foiling crossing that flies above the chop — smoother, quieter and far more weather-resilient, so the trip actually runs on schedule.

journeys.today: Wooden longboats and diesel day-boats weave between reefs at low speed, with noise and wake inside a protected marine park.
journeys.with_navier: A quiet, wake-light foiling hop of a few nautical miles, clearing shallow reef approaches in low-foil mode with zero local emissions.

journeys.today: Fly to Semarang then transfer to a ferry — a full multi-modal day eaten by connections and weather.
journeys.with_navier: A single long-range hybrid passage across the calm interior Java Sea — no charging infrastructure required at the island end.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: The whole working network sits in range: intra-archipelago hops of 3–10 nm, and the mainland gateway crossings from Semarang (~50 nm) and Jepara (~45 nm) both fall inside the 70 nm all-electric envelope — ideal for replacing the weather-fragile ferry on the routes that carry the volume today.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: The long mainland-city runs — Jakarta (~280 nm) and Surabaya (~270 nm) direct across the sheltered interior Java Sea — exceed all-electric range and suit the long-range hybrid, which needs no shore-charging at the island end. This opens a same-day premium link no ferry offers.

competitive_landscape: The crossing is served today by conventional ferry operators — a private fast-ferry from Semarang (~2 hr) and the state slow ro-pax from Jepara (~6 hr) — plus wooden longboats for island day-trips. The pain is concrete: long journeys, frequent wet-season cancellations, and diesel boats operating inside a national marine park. The volume is real and seasonal; the experience is slow, fragile and undifferentiated, which is precisely the opening.
seasonality: The wet/northwest monsoon (Nov–Mar) brings afternoon squalls of 20–35 kt and 1.5–2.5 m swell on the open gateway legs, driving most ferry cancellations; the dry season (May–Oct) is the calm operating peak. The interior Java Sea has no typhoon track. Foiling flies above the short, steep chop that grounds conventional ferries, turning weather fragility into a reliability premium.
regulatory_note: Operations sit under a dual conservation mandate — Karimun Jawa National Park (KLHK Balai Taman Nasional, single park authority across all 27 islands) plus a Marine Protected Area (KKP) — which simplifies the intra-archipelago permitting to essentially one channel and gives a clean-fleet, low-wake quiet-mode operation a direct conservation rationale. Mainland gateway terminals fall under KSOP Semarang/Jepara and the Central Java provincial transport authority.
signature_routes: Karimun Besar ↔ Kemujan / Menjangan (clean intra-archipelago island-hopping)
Jakarta ↔ Karimunjawa (long-range direct escape across the interior Java Sea)

precedents.what: ~100-vessel, $100M phased clean-marine network with JIH Global, first 5 vessels in 2026
precedents.why_it_matters: Shows a full island-archipelago foiling network — gateway crossings plus protected intra-cluster hops — being financed and built at scale. The playbook to replicate for Java's marine-park archipelago.

deck_only.commercial_framing: Karimunjawa is the closest island cluster to the Jakarta/Surabaya wealth pool that sits cleanly inside long-range hybrid range over sheltered water. The 'mainland-city to diving paradise in one passage' line is a credible premium-charter product; near-term revenue base is the seasonal Semarang gateway flow plus the Kura Kura premium-resort segment.
deck_only.platform_split_rationale: Dual-platform market: all-electric leads the gateway crossings and intra-park hops (the volume); long-range hybrid is reserved strictly for the >70 nm mainland-city line-hauls and removes the island-end charging dependency.

internal.convener_notes: No active royal/sultanate overlay at the archipelago (Demak Sultanate extinct 1554; Yogyakarta/Solo Kratons are interior, not water-overlooking). Not a federal DPSP super-priority destination — standard line-ministry procurement cycle applies, no DPSP funding leverage. Kura Kura Resort (Italian ownership) is the only premium property; greenfield slot for a global luxury chain remains open. Cross-link: Jakarta is the long-range origin node, not a gateway-city.
internal.mro_note: Best composite-MRO proximity of the Indonesian island files — Banyuwangi composite cluster ~180 nm — a material fleet-economics advantage if Java-Sea-north scales.
